subject: Future Tech
title: FDM: The Desktop Standard
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: FDM: The Desktop Standard.

hook.text: Fused Deposition Modeling melts plastic filament and squeezes it through a hot nozzle, drawing each layer like icing.

buildup.text: A motor feeds filament, the nozzle draws molten plastic, and the bed steps down one layer at a time.

discovery.text: FDM is the most popular consumer 3D printing method. Printers start under $200 and use spools of PLA or ABS plastic.

twist.text: FDM prints show visible layer lines and are weaker along the Z-axis. Between layers is always the weakest point.

climax.text: Despite limitations, FDM dominates education, prototyping, and hobbyist markets.

punchline.text: A hot nozzle and melted plastic built a revolution.

quiz.question: What is the weakest direction in an FDM-printed part?
